tldr: Across all 10 regional headline sets, the dominant advertised story is Spain enacting emergency sheltering and relocation policy in response to the Ceuta surge; Russian state-media headlines are the only ones to pivot to enforcement and sovereignty, and German coverage alone names child-protection risk in its headline.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame Spain's children policy as an 'immigration U-turn', signalling a reversal invisible to readers of all other outlets.
Only headline to name child abuse as an explicit risk, surfacing the protection-failure angle that every other outlet's headline omits.
Only headline to leave Ceuta entirely, reporting a French Channel-crossing interception — giving RT readers a pan-European border-crisis frame no other headline provides.
Only headline to foreground Morocco's sovereignty claim over Ceuta and Melilla, elevating a diplomatic dispute that no other outlet's headline mentions.

bottom_line: Headline coverage sells the Ceuta crisis as a Spanish policy story — shelters built, children relocated — while Russian state-media headlines alone pivot to enforcement and sovereignty, and the deaths that body-text coverage treats as central appear only in pan-African and Canadian outlet titles.
